RC8 repairs automatic context delivery in linked worktrees and removes preparation work that
could exhaust the operation allowance before JEV selection began.

- Hook readiness now checks Codex's main-checkout definition source separately from each
  worktree's runtime. Linked installation rejects an incomplete shared-hook cutover before writes.
  Repair the main checkout deliberately, then reconcile active worktrees at a safe seam. Review
  changed hooks through normal host trust; an on-disk check does not prove native delivery.
- Changed-file capture uses bulk Git metadata. Bounded index freshness checks avoid scanning
  unrelated binary assets and leave room for incremental extraction. All eligible paths remain
  visible. Uncertain sources require literal bytes; current-source checks and fallback remain.
- Native prompt delivery follows an explicitly declared route total, including framing and skills;
  profiles without an explicit total keep the 24,000-byte native default.
  Doctor detects required-context overflow in declared routes and bounded mixed-owner scenarios.
  Profile corrections remain deliberate. Required guidance cannot be silently discarded.
- Receipts separate source capture and index phases, so preparation cost and stalled refreshes
  can be diagnosed without confusing them with provider latency.

Existing JEV sharing permissions, optional enablement and the fixed coding model remain project-owned.
Provider calls and installed probes do not establish token savings or accepted development outcomes.
Computer-use automation is deferred.

Publication uses the locally qualified archive and independent implementation review, following the
operator's local-validation workflow. GitHub Actions is skipped for this publication; it remains
enabled for later work. Local proof does not establish Linux-host behavior, physical-device results
or successful native adoption in another checkout.
